newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-TRAPATTONI WANTS TO STAY AT BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TRAPATTONI WANTS TO STAY AT BAYERN.

text.p: Giovanni Trapattoni intends to remain coach of Bayern Munich for another season. He also dismissed rumours in Italy of a move to Roma, an Italian newspaper reported on Thursday.
"I gave my word to people who respect me and value me. A two-year contract and two years it will be. Unless they kick me out. Unless we don't win anything, " he was quoted as saying by Tuttosport.
"Or unless they have already approached someone else only because in Italy people say too much and make too many mistakes -- they make it up for the pleasure of making it up."

Trapattoni, Italy's most successful coach, joined Bayern at the start of the season after a previous stint at the German club in 1994-95 which was not a great success. He won the Italian league title six times as Juventus coach and once while in charge of Internazionale.

Italian newspapers speculated last year that Trapattoni would replace former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi at the helm of the national team, reporting that Cesare Maldini might be asked to keep the seat warm until the end of the season.
But Maldini was given a contract to the 1998 World Cup finals and his side has yet to be beaten or concede a goal.
After Roma sacked Argentine Carlos Bianchi last week, Trapattoni has again been repeatedly talked of as the likely new incumbent at the club from next season.
Trapattoni said that a man such as Albertino Bigon, currently coaching at Swiss side Sion and who took Napoli to the league title in 1990, would be a good choice.

"I only need to carry out the work as I have planned it," Trapattoni said. "Win the championship and then start the Champions' League adventure next season with a team that can at least hope to pull it off."
Trapattoni also commented on rumours linking Bayern's departing striker Juergen Klinsmann to Italian side Parma.
"Parma? I don't know, it sounds odd. Klinsmann has a stupendous villa on Lake Como (north of Milan) and that's where he intends to live," the coach said.
Gazzetta dello Sport reported on Thursday that Parma were after Klinsmann, who spent three seasons at Inter from 1989 to 1992 when Trapattoni was the coach there.
The paper said that the club, also on course for a Champions' League slot as second-placed team in the league, had reached a deal with the striker but not yet signed it.
It said coach Carlo Ancelotti had yet to approve it and Klinsmann was likely to be used as a reinforcement for regular players rather than as a first choice player.
